facts.value: The FSAG Annual Treasury Management Report to Audit and Scrutiny on 19 March 2026 is a covering/governance return — 4 pages of process narrative with no numbers, plus three appendices which are the printed minutes of the three FSAG meetings held over the year. The substantive treasury reports FSAG actually considered (2024/25 Outturn, 2025/26 Mid-Year, 2026/27 TMS) are named as background papers with URLs but not attached to this report and not held by us.

source.title: FSAG Annual Treasury Management Report — Appendix 3 (minutes of FSAG 30 January 2026)

summary.text:
The paper is thin by design — it is FSAG's annual governance return to Audit and Scrutiny, agreed at Full Council in July 2023 as the mechanism by which FSAG reports back on its delegated monitoring of the treasury function. The covering report (4pp) carries no figures. The three appendices are the printed minutes of the three FSAG meetings held over the year (26 September 2025 on the 2024/25 Outturn; 21 November 2025 on the 2025/26 Mid-Year; 30 January 2026 on the 2026/27 Treasury Management and Investment Strategy).

Only three concrete treasury-related figures appear across the four PDFs: treasury investment balance £23.2m at March 2024 falling to £19.8m at March 2025 (Appendix 1 p.2); three fixed-term deposits held at 21 November 2025 with one matured end October and moved to a Money Market Fund, two others maturing April and September 2026 (Appendix 2 p.1); and a council tax rise of 2.98% / £6.93 Band D for 2026/27 agreed 3-2 (Appendix 3 p.2). No CFR, no external borrowing figure, no MRP, no prudential indicator, no maturity structure limit, no authorised limit, no liability benchmark. The S151's line at §5.1 of the covering report — 'Treasury performance continues to operate within the limits and indicators approved by Full Council and no compliance issues have been identified' — is the paper's own summary of substance.

The loan-book reconciliation cannot be run against this paper because the paper publishes no borrowing figure. Separately, our PWLB file shows Epsom and Ewell with five loans totalling £64,426,560 at a weighted 2.5227% (four MATURITY loans at ~42 years and 2.44%-2.68%, one £5m at 2.200% in the 1-2 year bucket) — arrived on the file between October 2025 and February 2026 against a starting position of zero PWLB debt at 30 June 2025. The rates on the four long loans are inconsistent with the PWLB certainty rates that would have been printed in Oct-Nov 2025 or February 2026 (50-year gilt was ~4.74% per the 22 December 2025 Arlingclose forecast, implying certainty rates around 5.5% at that tenor). Recorded here as an internal data question rather than a finding, and outreach is not appropriate until the file provenance is resolved.

No email drafted. This is the correct outcome for the paper: a covering governance return with no treasury figures worth writing to an S151 about, plus a data anomaly that needs investigating our end before any Epsom & Ewell outreach.
